original_record.question:
This piece of paper was folded in half twice, and then had two equilateral triangles cut out of it. Which diagram shows how the paper will look when it is unfolded again? <image1>
<image2>
original_record.solution: The diagram shows how the cut-out triangles form rhombic holes when the paper is unfolded. ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-009.jpg?height=212&width=209&top_left_y=508&top_left_x=1529)

audit.explicit_conditions:
This piece of paper was folded in half twice, and then had two equilateral triangles cut out of it. Which diagram shows how the paper will look when it is unfolded again? <image1>
<image2>

answer_review.reasoning: Use quarter coordinates x in[0,1],y in[0,1], with fold edges x=0 and y=1. Reflect each triangular notch across its fold edge, then across the other crease. The left-edge notch produces two wide horizontal rhombi at the top/bottom of the unfolded square; the top-edge notch produces two tall vertical rhombi at left/right. No cut reaches the intersection of folds, so no central hole occurs. Only C has this arrangement.

audit.display_conditions: Semantic paper fill gray, cutouts white; outlines black1pt. Options preserve orientation distinctions, not merely hole counts. Projection, hinge angle and exact edge-occlusion subdivision frozen independently.
source_artifact_exclusions: Blue imageN headers and separator rules are dataset packaging, not the question figure.
audit.native_model: 3D coordinates, rigid folded paper / wood model, explicit projection and boundary visibility. Native analytic vector objects only.
